summary: W4A16 MoE decode on NVFP4-CSF checkpoints now runs as fast as plain NVFP4, and GLM-5.3 runs W4A16 at TP6 (352 expert channels per rank)
compatibility: No user action required. CSF scale memory is unchanged by default; B12X_NVFP4_CSF_INLINE_WORDS=32 (the GLM-5.3 profile) spends about 25% of the native scale bytes more on records with inline replacement words.
details: Stage-readable NVFP4-CSF scale storage no longer needs a per-tile prologue wait or reads that depend on the previous stage: each tile stages its exception records while its route block is read, every stage copies its codes and replacement-word window together, and the scale-word rebuild overlaps the stage's MMAs; outputs stay bit-identical to native NVFP4 scales.

B12X_NVFP4_CSF_INLINE_WORDS (read when the CSF experts are prepared) puts that many replacement words inline in each 128-row record (64-row records: five eighths of it); the default 0 keeps 32-byte records, the memory of the previous storage.
Served GLM-5.3 TP8 MTP3 with 32 inline words: the FP4-CSF checkpoint decodes within 1.5% of the original (C1 83.9 vs 85.0, C2 137.3 vs 138.7, C4 194.9 vs 196.8 steps/s).

Packed NVFP4 W4A16 (native and CSF scales) supports expert shards whose channel count is 32 mod 64, such as GLM-5.3 TP6 (2048 padded to 2112, 352 channels per rank): N64 gate/up tiles and K32 down tiles, for decode and prefill.
Fixes a K32 activation-tile swizzle that left its 64-byte rows and corrupted large-batch outputs of K32 W4A16 tiles.
